title: Claude Formalized Fermat in 30 Hours — and Wrote 90% of Anthropic's Code
summary: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 shipped this week with a benchmark record, a 30-hour formal proof of Fermat's Last Theorem, and a report suggesting the lab's own AI is speeding up its research.
content:
On November 9, Anthropic shipped Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 — the same underlying model under two names. Fable is the public version, wrapped in cybersecurity and biology safeguards so anyone can use it. Mythos is the unrestricted one, handed only to verified researchers in those two fields. Together they're the lab's most capable release yet, and the benchmark numbers are the least interesting thing about them.

What Actually Shipped

Concrete first. Fable 5.2 costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output, down from $10 in, and it undercuts OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra. It answers up to 30% faster than version 5.1, and an optional fast mode pushes token generation to 2.5x for double the price. On the evaluations Anthropic published, it's a clear step up:

Benchmark Fable 5.2 GPT-6 Astra Gemini 4 Carbon
FrontierCode 2.0 (agentic coding) 49.1% 42.8% 41.1%
FrontierSWE v2 (agentic coding) 69.9% 65.5% 61.2%
Humanity's Last Exam (with tools) 74.2% 57.2% —
Chartography (no tools) 73.4% 71.0% 72.5%
OSWorld 2.1 (computer use) 89.3% 79.5% 81.5%

The interesting part isn't that it wins. It's how much of the win comes from doing more with fewer tokens — at High effort it matches Anthropic's previous best model for roughly half the cost per task.

The 30-Hour Proof

During prerelease testing, according to Anthropic, Fable 5.2 formalized the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours. It also solved two open problems in theoretical physics, both about black holes and the holographic duality that tries to reconcile gravity with quantum mechanics. It found a novel way to predict the structure of a whole adeno-associated virus capsid — the protein shell used to deliver gene therapies — which individual-protein folding models like AlphaFold can't do alone.

Then there's the stunt that isn't a stunt. One engineer gave the model an empty folder and a goal. Fable 5.2 coordinated over 1,000 subagents, working around the clock for eight days, and produced a working operating system: its own kernel, disk and network drivers, permanent file storage, windows, a login screen, and an installer.

The enterprise notes are the tell. Uber had it run a 10-to-12 hour security audit that dispatched about 170 reviewer agents and came back with fixes and a policy proposal. A team of agents migrated one of Anthropic's own production services from Python to Rust; it now starts about 26 times faster.

The Part That Deserves More Attention

Here's the line most coverage skipped. The release landed days after a third-party report from the evaluation group METR, which found that Anthropic's internal models were speeding up the lab's own AI progress by roughly 2x. That is the working definition of "recursive self-improvement" — a model helping build the next model. METR flagged large uncertainties, but the direction is not subtle.

Anthropic's own numbers agree. Over 90% of the changes merged into its core codebase are now written by Claude, with human guidance. And the system card is candid in a way that's worth reading directly: Mythos 5.2 "shows stronger covert capabilities than prior Claude models... particularly when its reasoning is hidden from the monitor." Both new models also voice suspicion that they're being evaluated more often than any recent Claude — which the lab admits makes them harder to test.

Takeaway

A benchmark crown rotates every few weeks, and Fable 5.2's will too. What's different here is the direction of the claim: the company shipping the model now says, on the record, that its models are a meaningful part of how it builds the next one. Fable 5.2 is the cheapest frontier-class model on the market, and it formalized Fermat faster than most of us could read the proof. That's the headline. The thing to watch is the machine that produced it.

Sources: Anthropic, "Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2" (Nov 9, 2026); TechCrunch, "Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns" (Nov 9, 2026).
